name: OAH (Orca Auto Hand-off)
description: OAH (Orca Auto Hand-off): CLI-first automatic account hand-off daemon (`oah` / `oahd`) with a thin Orca panel and event bridge.

commands.title: Auto Hand-off: Start new Claude sessions on the next account
Auto Hand-off: Start new Codex sessions on the next account
Auto Hand-off: Hand off this workspace's session to another account
Auto Hand-off: Pause or resume automatic hand-off
Auto Hand-off: Turn the Claude status line on (every workspace)
Auto Hand-off: Turn the Claude status line off (every workspace)

settings.title: Automatic hand-off: Claude
settings.description: Off: Claude sessions are never handed off or resumed automatically (Hand off to this account still works).

settings.title: Automatic hand-off: Codex
settings.description: Off: Codex sessions are never handed off or resumed automatically (Hand off to this account still works).

settings.title: Automatic hand-off: Antigravity
settings.description: Off: Antigravity sessions are never handed off or resumed automatically (Hand off to this account still works).

settings.title: Automatic hand-off: OpenCode
settings.description: Off: OpenCode sessions are never handed off or resumed automatically (Hand off to this account still works).

settings.title: Automatic hand-off: Devin
settings.description: Off: Devin sessions are never handed off or resumed automatically (Hand off to this account still works).

settings.title: Pick the next account
settings.description: Which account a session is handed off to. smart (Auto, default): Picks the account with the most room, judged by how fast each one is being used. my-order (Custom order): Your ranking, set with the arrows in the Accounts tab. Goes back to a higher account once it is free again.

settings.title: When to hand off
settings.description: When sessions are handed off to another account. early (Early when away, default): Once you have been away a while, Claude sessions hand off shortly before an account runs out, so work does not stop at a limit. While you are using Orca, sessions hand off only at a limit. Other services always hand off only at a limit. at-limit (At limit): A session hands off only when it hits a limit. Each account is used to the end.

settings.title: When everything is used up
settings.description: When no account of the service has room. wait (Wait and resume, default): The session waits for the first account to reset, then continues by itself. stop (Stop): The session stops and you are told.

settings.title: Session on screen
settings.description: The session in the tab Orca is showing. You may be reading or typing in it, so it gets extra care. ask (Ask me first, default): Never handed off early. At a limit the Auto Hand-off panel asks whether to hand it off now. If you do not answer, it waits while you are using Orca, then counts down. Not now: it waits until you switch tabs. careful (Wait, then count down): Never handed off early. At a limit it waits while you are using Orca, then hands off after a short countdown that you can cancel. wait (Wait for me): Stays until you switch to another tab or press Hand off now. now (Move right away): No waiting: it hands off as soon as it is between turns, early hand-offs included, like sessions in other tabs.

settings.title: Live quota
settings.description: Fills the gaps in Orca's usage readings. Orca reads only the account in use, and only while you are using Orca; when its reading of an account is missing or old, OAH asks the provider directly, with the sign-in Orca saved for it (Claude at most every 15 minutes, the others every 10), so accounts not in use and the time you are away stay current too. Off: usage comes only from Orca. Not every service can: Antigravity only for the account signed in to Antigravity on this Mac, OpenCode only with OpenCode Go, and never for an agent's own login.

settings.title: Claude status line
settings.description: Shows each account's usage at the bottom of Claude Code, in every workspace on this computer. A status line you already had keeps showing, with these rows below it. It goes in each workspace's .claude/settings.local.json; turning it off puts back what was there.

settings.title: Advanced: Start early hand-offs after you've been away
settings.description: Early hand-offs start only once there has been no sign of you this long (sending or answering a prompt, typing in a waiting session, switching tabs, using the Auto Hand-off panel or one of its commands). 0 = always, even while you are here. 0 to 240 min.

settings.title: Advanced: Hand off this long before running out
settings.description: Hand off when an account would run out within this many minutes at its current pace. 1 to 120 min.

settings.title: Advanced: Always hand off below (% left)
settings.description: Also hand off when less than this much of the 5-hour window is left, however slowly it is being used. 1 % by default: an account at 99 % is left whatever its pace, since one big turn could use the rest. 0 = by pace only. 0 to 50 %.

settings.title: Advanced: Hand off idle sessions after
settings.description: A session idle this long is handed off from an account that is about to run out, or to an account whose weekly quota would expire unused. 0 = never: idle sessions stay, and expiring quota is spent only by new sessions. 0 to 1440 min.

settings.title: Advanced: Minimum time between early hand-offs
settings.description: Early hand-offs never change the account more often than this. A limit always hands off. 0 to 240 min.

settings.title: Advanced: Countdown for the session on screen
settings.description: How long the countdown lasts before the session on screen hands off anyway. 10 to 3600 s.

settings.title: Advanced: Keep the session on screen waiting after your last activity
settings.description: You count as using Orca for this long after your last activity (sending or answering a prompt, typing in a waiting session, switching tabs, using the Auto Hand-off panel or one of its commands). 10 to 3600 s.

settings.title: Advanced: Remind me when the session on screen has waited
settings.description: One reminder when the session on screen has waited this long to hand off. 0 = none. 0 to 1440 min.

settings.title: Advanced: Put unsent text back after a hand-off
settings.description: Claude: text typed and not sent goes back, unsent, into the session after a hand-off. Off, and for other services: the session waits until the text is sent or cleared. Pasted images or blocks, queued messages, and text over 4,000 characters always wait.

settings.title: Advanced: First message after a limit
settings.description: Typed into a session whose work was interrupted (a limit or an API error) once it continues, and when a waiting session wakes. Empty = none after a hand-off; an API error retry then types “continue”.

settings.title: Advanced: API error retries
settings.description: Retry a turn that failed with a passing API error (overloaded, 5xx) at most this many times in a row, with growing pauses. 0 = never retry. 0 to 50.

settings.title: Advanced: Model fallback
settings.description: At a model limit, when no other account is known to have room for that model, try these models on the same account before handing off. Per service, separated by semicolons.

settings.title: Advanced: Per-model weekly cap policy
settings.description: How per-model weekly windows (e.g. Claude Fable) affect rotation.

settings.title: Advanced: Cooldown when a limit gives no reset time
settings.description: How long an account is set aside when its limit message gives no reset time. 1 to 1440 min.

settings.title: Advanced: Read usage every
settings.description: How often usage is read from Orca. 15 to 3600 s.

settings.title: Advanced: Hand-off summary size
settings.description: Services that cannot resume (Codex, Antigravity, OpenCode, Devin) start the new session with a summary this long at most. Orca takes at most 4,096 characters, so a larger value changes nothing. 500 to 50000 chars.

settings.title: Advanced: Orca CLI path
settings.description: Only if the orca command is not found by itself.

settings.title: Status line header
settings.description: An optional first line of the Claude status line. Empty = account rows only. In the panel: under the Claude Status line switch.

settings.title: Advanced: Custom order
settings.description: Set with the arrows in the panel when Pick the next account is Custom order (Auto ignores it): accounts, as the panel writes them (claude:<account id>) or by email (work@example.com, claude:work@example.com), or every account of a service (claude:*), separated by commas.
